chapter: Opinions, Edgar Battle and closing stories
title: Eddie Barefield: teaching and circus work

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Oh yeah. You mentioned Eddy Heartfield.
Oh God, he's great, a great musician. I remember when he was on staff at NBC, all the saxophone players wanted to study with Eddie. He's doing, he's teaching

now there at Charlie Coven's studios in New York. And he's also doing a Circus and he just got back, Ivan Rollé told me, bass player from LA, think he did a recording date under his name for the Harry Lim label.
Yeah, I'm told he's playing mostly tenor now.

Yeah, tenor. And Ivan said to me, he says, Oh, Cozy, Eddie's talking about that saxophone's a faggot's instrument. So Ivan said to him, he said, was Cannonball Adderly a faggot, or was Charlie Parker a faggot, and Eddie said 'No, well they were exceptions.' So he's playing tenor now. But he's a great musician.
He was a great lead alto player.
Yeah, he was way back there with Fletcher Henderson, McKenny's Cotton Pickers. He does the Ringling Brothers Circus every year. Is that the Ringling Brothers Circus that you did?
Yeah, just finished doing a couple of weeks with them in Washington.
Did it go to New York then?
They spend, there's two different road companies and they spend, I guess one of them spends ten weeks a year at Madison Square Garden, one of the two, and they hire guys from New York.
Eddie's been doing that for the past four or five years. They pay good money on those things.
It's pretty gruelling though, you earn your money. But yeah. I'm told he's a big bruiser of a guy.
